options.text: Frost, liquid water, and breath mist are different states of the same substance, water.
Frost, liquid water, and breath mist are three different substances, not water at all.
Only the liquid in the bottle is water; frost and breath mist are unrelated solids and gases.
Breath mist is a different substance from frost because one looks white and the other looks clear when melted.

stem: Bilal notices frost on the freezer door, liquid water in a steel bottle, and mist from his breath on a cold morning. Which statement is correct?

teacher.key_rationale: Ice/frost, liquid water, and water vapour/mist are states of water, not different substances. Appearance alone does not make them different substances.
